<note>original: "shengqi" refers to vital energy or life force</note>

As for that which cannot be divided, consider the practitioners of internal cultivation <note>referring to Neidan or internal alchemy</note> who regard essence, energy, and spirit <note>original: "jing, qi, shen"</note> as the Three Treasures. In the state of Pre-heaven <note>referring to the innate or primordial state before birth</note>, energy is transformed through spirit into energy, and energy is transformed into essence. In the state of Post-heaven <note>referring to the acquired state after birth</note>, energy is transformed through essence into energy, and energy is transformed into spirit. The generative transformations of these three serve as mutual roots for one another, as they are ultimately the same single energy <note>term: qi</note>. This is why they are considered indivisible. Therefore, those skilled at treating essence can cause energy to be produced from within essence, and those skilled at treating energy can cause essence to be produced from within energy. This is the wondrous application of that which can and cannot be divided. Furthermore, regarding the Yin and Yang of cold and heat, these absolutely must be divided. For the nature of cold is like ice, while the nature of heat is like charcoal. Since ice and charcoal cannot coexist or be used for the same purpose, how can they be applied recklessly? Thus I say: the Yin and Yang of essence and energy cannot be separated, but the Yin and Yang of cold and heat must not be confused. This is the most vital and definitive principle for physicians.
